To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the carbonyl group in inosine is a good nucleophilic center for the phosphitylation reaction; 2) inosine phosphoramidite can be synthesized by using the phosphitylation method; and 3) inosine 3'-O-phosphoramidite can serve as a good precursor to synthesize the inosine 2'-, 3'- and 5'-O-phosphorothioates.

1) The phosphitylation of inosine carbonyl oxygen was achieved by using a phosphoramidite activated with a non-nucleophilidic acidic activator; 2) The phosphitylated inosine derivative was successfully used in oligonucleotide synthesis.

the phosphitylation of inosine derivatives with phosphoramidites, activated with non-nucleophilidic acidic activators, provides a new synthetic method of inosine nucleosides with the 6-phosphodiester group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of inosine derivatives bearing an O-6 phosphodiester group.
the development of new strategies to prepare nucleoside phosphoramidites for the synthesis of nucleoside diesters.
the synthesis of inosine derivatives bearing the phosphodiester group in the O(6) position of the nucleobases and the synthesis of oligonucleotides containing these derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the synthesis of inosine derivatives bearing phosphodiester groups at the O(5)-position of the ribose unit and at the O(3)- and O(6)-positions of the nucleobases is feasible via phosphitylation reactions of the corresponding carbonyl groups.

the use of non-nucleophillic acidic activators is not suitable for the phosphitylation of carbonyl oxygen in the presence of the nucleobases, but the phosphitylation reaction can be successfully conducted in the absence of nucleobases.
the carbonyl group of the nucleobases is not an inert group in terms of chemical reactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we could successfully synthesize inosine derivatives bearing phosphodiester groups at the O(3) and O(5) position of the nucleobases.
the phosphitylation of a carbonyl oxygen can be used as a new method for the introduction of a phosphodiester linkage.

we have shown that phosphoramidites can be used as phosphorylating agents for carbonyl groups in the presence of a suitable acidic activator, and that this reaction can be extended to the synthesis of inosine nucleotides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carbonyl group of the pyrimidine nucleobase can be selectively phosphitylated in the presence of other nucleophilic functional groups.
phosphoramidite activated by non-nucelophic acidic activators can react with carbonyl oxygen to form a phosphodiester.
it is possible to use phosphoramidites to activate a carbonyl oxygen for phosphodiester formation, thus providing a new route to nucleoside 6-phosphate derivatives.
